subject: Hosted API: proposed monthly commit uplift + ops & contract path
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Mills <sara@parcelly.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-04-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Hosted API: proposed monthly commit uplift + ops & contract path

Sara / Tom —

Thanks again for the conversation this morning. Parcelly’s seasonal traffic profile lines up well with a stepped monthly commit instead of a single flat uplift; attached is a draft IO that shows a 3-tier monthly commit for the next 9 months (baseline + two staged increases) plus an optional burst bucket. High level ask from us: confirm whether Parcelly can sign a 9-month stepped commit (starts May 1st) and whether finance can accept monthly invoicing vs. net-30 on a consolidated invoice.

From an ops perspective, two items to confirm before we push to legal/finance:
- Rate limits per route: Parcelly told us they have two heavy routes (tracking ingestion + user chat). We should pin a per-route soft throttle table to avoid noisy neighbors.
- SLA window for burst: they want short bursts during EU morning hours — we should confirm region routing for those windows.

I've CC'd Vanessa for renewal commercial and Marissa for the billing path. Karthik — can you confirm the recommended soft throttle bands and whether a fallback smaller model is required for predictable SLOs?

Next steps I propose:
1) Parcelly confirms billing cadence and who signs (Sara / Tom)
2) Internal: legal review of the IO + standard SOW (I'll prep a canary clause for burst overage)
3) DocuSign goes out with a 72-hour review window so we can hit the May 1 start

Attachment: parcelly_uplift_draft_IO_20280418.pdf (draft pricing table + staged commits)

Thanks —
Jordan
Jordan Blake
Account Exec, Customer Growth
Redwood Inference

From: Sara Mills <sara@parcelly.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Li <tom.li@parcelly.com>
Date: 2028-04-18T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API: proposed monthly commit uplift + ops & contract path

Jordan —

Appreciate the quick follow-up and the draft IO. A few clarifying questions from our side before we take to procurement:

1) Can you confirm effective per-token rates once we step into the second and third tiers (we need the blended unit price for internal forecasting)?
2) For throttles: what happens when we hit the soft throttle? Is it queued, rejected, or routed to a cheaper model? We need to understand impact to latency for customer-facing chat.
3) Billing cadence: finance prefers net-30 consolidated invoices; however, the procurement team may ask for an annual PO. Is there flexibility to accept either monthly invoice or a single PO that references monthly commits?

Timing: procurement needs the legal-ready IO and a list of SLAs and liability caps to start their review next week. Can you get legal-ready docs over by EOD Tuesday? We can then route to procurement for a 5–7 business day turnaround.

Also, we’d like to see the throughput profile for the chat route to validate the burst window — could you send the last 90 days of peak-per-minute metrics (or an ops summary)?

Thanks —
Sara
Director of Product Ops
Parcelly Inc.

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Sara Mills <sara@parcelly.com>
Date: 2028-04-19T10:25:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API: proposed monthly commit uplift + ops & contract path

Jordan / team / Sara —

Quick technical summary to answer Sara’s throttling and routing questions:

- Soft throttle behavior: we apply a backpressure policy that prefers immediate rejection with a 429 for non-essential background routes, and queuing for low-latency chat where queueing remains under the configured latency SLO. We can also configure automatic fallback routing to a smaller, lower-cost model (e.g., redwood-small-int8) when queue depth exceeds threshold to preserve request success rate while degrading quality gracefully.

- Blended pricing: based on the staged commit in the attached IO, blended per-token cost for month 2 (mid-tier) comes to $0.0017/token and month 3 (highest-tier) to $0.0014/token (these are blended after applying burst credit amortization). We’ll include the blended math in the legal-ready IO.

- Ops: for the EU morning burst window we recommend pinning routing to a EU region pool with a dedicated burst lane (we can reserve a small dedicated capacity in May to avoid cold-start latency). That avoids cross-region routing.

Attached: throughput-profiles-apr2028.png (summary of 90-day peaks and 95th percentile per-minute)

If Parcelly wants to keep user-chat latency under 250ms p95 during bursts we should:
- Enable auto-fallback to smaller model at 85% slot utilization
- Reserve a 10% burst cushion on top of committed throughput for the first 60 days

I’ll draft the exact soft-throttle table and include the model fallback clause for legal.

—Karthik
Principal Solutions Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Mills <sara@parcelly.com>, Tom Li <tom.li@parcelly.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-04-20T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API: proposed monthly commit uplift + ops & contract path

Sara / Tom —

Thanks — this is actionable. Summary of agreed next steps so we’re aligned:

1) Legal-ready IO: Redwood will send a finalized IO by EOD Tuesday (includes blended pricing table, soft throttle definitions, model-fallback clause, and a 9-month stepped commit schedule).
2) Billing: Parcelly can indicate preference for monthly invoicing or provide a single PO referencing the monthly commits. Either path is acceptable — finance will honor net-30.
3) Ops: Redwood will reserve a small EU burst lane for May (10% cushion) and apply the auto-fallback rule at 85% utilization for chat routes. Karthik to attach the exact soft-throttle table in the IO.
4) Signature timeline: we’ll push DocuSign to your team once legal-ready IO is confirmed; signed within 72 hours gets a prorated May 1 start and immediate capacity reservation.

We’ll send the DocuSign link + HubSpot deal update when the IO is ready. For reference: HubSpot deal PL-2028-0478; DocuSign link (will be live with the IO): https://www.docusign.com/secure-link/1a2b3c4d

Jordan
Account Exec, Customer Growth
Redwood Inference
Attachment: parcelly_uplift_draft_IO_20280418.pdf (updated after legal review)
